ai.title: Remove agent store grid animations
ai.summary: Removes layout and entry animations from agent store grids in web/src/app/store/page.tsx. Replaced motion.div with standard div and stripped initial/animate props from card containers to reduce sluggishness. Hover effects remain intact.

eli5.text: When you open the agent store page, the grid of agent cards no longer fades or slides in one by one as the page loads. Instead, all the cards appear immediately when the page loads, making the page feel less sluggish. The cards still gently lift up when you hover over them with your mouse. This change is live today and affects anyone viewing the agent store page.

ai.title: Add partial indexes to agentrun for completed status
ai.summary: Migration 0029 adds four partial b-tree indexes to agent_run filtered on status = 'completed'. Covers publisher/agent name, recent creation order, version lookup, and user_id. Scope limited to common/src/db/migrations and schema.ts. Indexes use CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS to ensure idempotent application.

eli5.text: The agent store page now loads list views much faster when you browse completed agents. The system added targeted indexes that act like sorted filing tabs for already-finished agents, so the database skips the slow full table search and pulls results by agent name, publisher, version, or your own completed runs instead. You can scroll and filter the completed agent list without waiting on long loading pauses, and the lookup for your past runs shows up quicker when you open the store.

ai.title: Add Copy ID and Run Agent CTAs to agent detail and store pages
ai.summary: Added `CopyIdButton` and `RunAgentButton` components to the agent version detail page, replacing the inline `EnhancedCopyButton` and raw code snippet. The `RunAgentButton` copies `codebuff --agent <id>` to the clipboard via `navigator.clipboard.writeText` and triggers a toast notification. A similar copy-command button was added to the agent store list cards in `web/src/app/store/page.tsx`. Changes are scoped to the Web frontend, specifically `web/src/app/publishers/[id]/agents/[agentId]/[version]/` and the store page.

eli5.text: When you view a specific version of an agent in the web interface, you will now see two buttons: one that copies the agent's ID to your clipboard, and another that copies the full command needed to run that agent (like 'codebuff --agent <id>'). If you visit the public agent store, each agent card will also show a button that copies the same run command. These buttons save you from having to manually find and retype the correct command each time you want to launch an agent.

ai.title: Remove keepDuringTruncation override in agent step loop
ai.summary: Removed explicit mapping of `keepDuringTruncation: false` for initial message history in `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`. The loop now spreads `agentState.messageHistory` directly into `initialMessages`. This relies on existing state properties rather than forcing the flag to false during history construction.

eli5.text: When the assistant goes to work on a task, it pulls in the conversation history to keep track of what's already happened. The program used to force one bookkeeping flag to a specific value while copying over the past messages. That forced setting has been removed, so the past messages are now copied in using their original flag values instead. You won't see this as a behavior change yourself, but it's a small piece of behind-the-scenes cleanup that makes how the assistant sets up its working memory more consistent.

ai.title: Refine Agent Store initial animation
ai.summary: Adjusted entry animations on `web/src/app/store/page.tsx`. Header fade replaced with targeted slide on publisher button; Editors Choice section wrapped in single fade to prevent layout shift during load. Publisher button logic updated to check `!publishers` alongside `!session`.

eli5.text: The change is live today for anyone using the Agent Store page. When the store page loads, the main heading area no longer uses a simple fade-in animation. Instead, only the "Publish Agent" button slides in with a slight delay, while the rest of the header loads statically to prevent the page from jumping around. The "Editor's Choice" section is now wrapped in a single fade animation instead of multiple nested ones to stop layout shifts during loading. The "Publish Agent" button will now also check if publisher information is available before showing, so signed-in users won't encounter errors when the data hasn't fully loaded yet.

ai.title: Store copy command includes full agent id
ai.summary: The store copy button now emits the fully-qualified command `codebuff --agent <publisher>/<id>@<version>` instead of the bare `codebuff --agent <id>`. The shortened form could not resolve uniquely when multiple publishers ship agents with the same id. Scoped to `web/src/app/store/page.tsx`; clipboard text, toast description, and button title all carry the full form.

eli5.text: When you visit the agent store and click the copy button to copy a run command, the text now puts into your clipboard a full command that includes both the publisher name and the agent version, like `codebuff --agent openai/summarizer@1.2.3`. Previously it copied just the agent name, such as `codebuff --agent summarizer`, which could be ambiguous if several publishers used the same agent name. You will notice the copied command contains more text, and any tooltip or confirmation message also reflects the full form. This applies to every agent listed on the store page whenever you use the copy action.

ai.title: Add messageHistoryLength to start event
ai.summary: Added messageHistoryLength field to the start event payload. Updated backend websocket action to include current history length. Extended common print-mode start schema to validate the new number type. Covers backend and shared type definitions.

eli5.text: When you start a conversation with the assistant, it now reports back how many previous messages are already stored in that conversation's history. This only affects the behind-the-scenes signal that kicks off a new assistant turn, it doesn't change what the assistant says or does during the chat. The number is now passed along as part of that starting message and the rule that checks it has been updated to expect a plain count.

ai.title: Stop spinner before tool call chunks
ai.summary: Spinner now stops before processing tool call chunks in npm-app/src/client.ts. Prevents visual artifact when streaming begins. Internal client logic only.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts streaming a response that includes tool use, the loading spinner now stops before the first chunk arrives, so you no longer see the spinner and the streamed text briefly at the same time. This only affects the internal client that powers the streaming interface; nothing about what gets streamed or how it is rendered changed.

ai.title: Remove version field from agent registry definitions
ai.summary: Dropped the `version: '1.0.0'` property from `AgentDefinition` objects in `.agents/registry/etl-manager.ts`, `extract-agent.ts`, `load-agent.ts`, and `transform-agent.ts`. Publisher attribution updated to `brandon` across these files. This simplifies the agent schema by removing redundant versioning for internal registry entries.

eli5.text: Internal agent definitions had their version numbers and publisher info tidied up. The version field was removed from four agent registry files, and publisher attribution was standardized to a single contributor across these files. You wouldn't notice any change in functionality - these are internal configuration files for automated agents, and the changes just clean up redundant versioning data that wasn't being actively used.

ai.title: New ETL agent registry
ai.summary: Added four new agent definitions to `.agents/registry`: `etl-manager.ts`, `extract-agent.ts`, `transform-agent.ts`, and `load-agent.ts`. These implement a sequential ETL pipeline (extract → transform → load) using `spawn_agents` and `handleSteps`. The manager uses `openai/gpt-5` while the workers use `anthropic/claude-4-sonnet-20250522`. Each agent defines specific `toolNames`, `instructionsPrompt`, and `inputSchema` for their stage.

eli5.text: A new four-part digital assistant has been added to the internal system, working together to fetch information from the web, clean and organize it, and then present the most useful results. Each part has its own specific role: one searches the web, another sorts and formats the data, and a third ranks everything based on what matters most to you. This assistant was assembled in September 2025 and is now available within the tool's agent registry, meaning you can use it today to run a complete search-and-filter workflow that previously required manual steps.

ai.title: Add image support to CLI and backend
ai.summary: CLI auto-detects image paths in prompts, processes them via `jimp` (compression/resizing), and sends structured `TextPart`/`ImagePart` content. Backend `loopAgentSteps` and `mainPrompt` updated to accept and merge this multi-part content into the agent message history. `npm-app/src/utils/image-handler.ts` introduced for image validation and encoding; `common/src/actions.ts` schema extended for optional `content` array. Limits: 2MB per file, 150KB base64 output.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question, you can now drop an image file path right into your message, the way you would attach a photo to an email. The tool you talk to will shrink and compress that image (up to about two megabytes) before sending the picture along with your text to the assistant, so you can ask questions about screenshots, diagrams, or photos instead of only typing. If you look closely at the new message you send, you will see a little paperclip note summarizing how many images were attached and their total size in kilobytes. This works today in the command line tool and the backend that powers it, with no special switch to flip.

ai.title: Codebuff 1.0.486 release bundle
ai.summary: Release 1.0.486 rolls up the batch of user-facing and internal work since 1.0.485 into the published `codebuff` package. Web surfaces gain the agent store copy-to-run refactor (emitting the fully-qualified `codebuff --agent <publisher>/<id>@<version>` command), publisher avatars, profile links, the TypeScript viewer for agent definitions, the BackButton component, and the Editor's Choice featuring `codebase-commands-explorer`. Backend/agent-loop changes include str-replace chaining and Windows newline fixes, messageHistoryLength on start events, partial DB indexes for completed agent runs, and a new `simple-code-reviewer` agent plus the ETL registry agents (`etl-manager`, `extract`/`transform`/`load`) using `openai/gpt-5` and `anthropic/claude-4-sonnet-20250522`. CLI adds image-prompt handling (2MB/file, 150KB base64 via jimp), base-lite now uses `openai/gpt-5` with medium reasoning, and the SDK ships colocated `index.d.ts` files.
ai.evidence: The diff for commit 7a0b4d10 shows a single-line version bump in `npm-app/release/package.json`, incrementing the `codebuff` package version from 1.0.485 to 1.0.486 with no other changes to the file or repository. Analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit ('Bump version to 1.0.486').

eli5.text: This release adds several new AI agents to the Codebuff store, including a code reviewer and an ETL pipeline manager, along with improvements to existing tools and the web interface. You can now see publisher avatars on the agent store and detail pages, copy full agent commands to your clipboard, and run agents directly from the store with a single click. The CLI now supports images in prompts, so you can include screenshots or diagrams when asking an agent to look at visual content. File editing has become more reliable, especially on Windows, and the agent step logging captures more detail for debugging. New walkthrough docs help you build and spawn your own agents, and a security policy file has been added for responsible vulnerability reporting.

ai.title: Require quotes for image paths with spaces
ai.summary: extractImagePaths now requires quotes for paths containing spaces to avoid false positives. Unquoted paths with spaces are no longer auto-detected. Updated tests in npm-app/src/__tests__/image-upload.test.ts reflect this stricter parsing behavior.

eli5.text: If you paste a file path that contains spaces without wrapping it in quotes, the system will no longer guess what file you meant. Instead, it waits for you to enclose the full path in quotes (like "My Documents/photo.png") before recognizing it as an image location. This stops the system from accidentally grabbing pieces of text that only look like file names.

ai.title: Refactor spinner lifecycle to stream handler
ai.summary: Moved `Spinner.get().start()` from `MarkdownStreamRenderer` to `client.ts` stream chunk handler, triggering on newline completion. Removed redundant `Spinner.get().stop()` calls in renderer flush/end methods and XML parser callback. Updated `printSubagentHeader` to restart 'Thinking' spinner for textless stopped states. Internal refactor affecting CLI display logic only.

eli5.text: You may notice the loading spinner next to your prompt is smoother and less jumpy as the assistant replies. Instead of the spinner starting and stopping at a few different moments, it now only resumes after each line of text finishes streaming in. This is purely a behind-the-scenes adjustment to how the spinner animation is managed during a response, so there's no new setting or option to use.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.487 with image path and spinner changes
ai.summary: The codebuff package manifest in npm-app/release/package.json moved from 1.0.486 to 1.0.487 with no source changes of its own. This release bundles a stricter image-path parser and a spinner-lifecycle refactor in the CLI display path. No user action is required; both changes ship as internal behavior updates alongside this bump.
ai.evidence: npm-app/release/package.json: version field bumped from 1.0.486 to 1.0.487 in the codebuff package manifest; release notes list two minor items, image path quoting strictness in extractImagePaths and spinner lifecycle relocation to client.ts stream handler.

eli5.text: This release sharpens the reliability of image handling and the on-screen experience while you work in the terminal. It now requires you to put quotes around image file names that contain spaces, which prevents the system from misreading those file locations as something else. The spinning loading indicator that appears while the tool thinks has been reworked so it starts and stops at more natural moments, such as when a line of text finishes streaming in, keeping the display smoother and less jittery. Together, these changes mean image uploads behave more predictably and the terminal interface stays cleaner and easier to follow during active work sessions.
